_comment: Course Study App — Recommended Readings (RR) Hierarchical Literature Index Template. If no literature is used, output '{}'. Keys are bare PDF filenames.

markdown_and_latex_support.note: ALL STRING FIELDS (title, author, description, outline[].title) SUPPORT FULL GITHUB-FLAVORED MARKDOWN AND KATEX MATH ($inline$ or $$display$$).
markdown_and_latex_support.mandatory_json_backslash_rule: CRITICAL: In JSON strings, the backslash '\' is the JSON escape character. Every LaTeX command MUST use double backslashes '\\'. For example, write '$\alpha$', '$\text{ms}$', '$$\frac{a}{b}$$', and '$O(M \times N)$'. Never write unescaped '\t' or '\f'. Escape literal dollar signs in prose as \$.
markdown_and_latex_support.code_and_math_rules: Use backticks (`$var`) exclusively for code, shell syntax, packet headers, and script variables; use dollar signs ($math$) exclusively for LaTeX math (never nest backticks in math). Never output raw HTML/MathML tags like <span class='katex'> or <math>. Escape literal dollar signs in prose as \$.

_schema_field_definitions.id: String. Unique kebab-case identifier used for internal system references and citations.
_schema_field_definitions.title: MARKDOWN & LATEX STRING FIELD. Full canonical title of the literature piece.
_schema_field_definitions.author: MARKDOWN & LATEX STRING FIELD. Authors, research group, or organization with publication year.
_schema_field_definitions.description: MARKDOWN & LATEX STRING FIELD. Brief synopsis (1-2 sentences) of the document's relevance.
_schema_field_definitions.total_slides: Integer. Total physical sheets/slides in the PDF file.
_schema_field_definitions.outline: Array of recursive Node objects representing chapters, sections, and structural parts.
_schema_field_definitions.outline[].title: MARKDOWN & LATEX STRING FIELD. Section, chapter, or topic title.
_schema_field_definitions.outline[].slides: Array of 2 Integers: [start_slide, end_slide]. 1-indexed inclusive PDF sheet bounds.
_schema_field_definitions.outline[].children: Array of Node objects (Optional). Arbitrarily nested sub-sections or sub-topics.
